title: Priority claim: independent sets of the three-row grid strip with the middle cell of every second column deleted - a sixth-order recurrence, Lean 4 formalized (AI4Math pipeline)
description: Priority claim of record (not a full paper). Contents: the claim note (LaTeX source + PDF), the Lean 4 sources (Lean v4.34.0, mathlib4 v4.34.0 rev 5ed29652; 0 sorry; #print axioms whitelist-checked) and the audit and novelty-search evidence. Result: z(n) counts the independent sets (empty set included) of the three-row by n-column grid strip P3 x P_n with the middle-row vertex of every odd-numbered column deleted (0-based columns 1,3,5,...); the kernel layer proves the sixth-order recurrence z(n) + 15 z(n-4) = 12 z(n-2) + 2 z(n-6) for all n >= 6 (natural-number truncated subtraction, self-consistent under the hypothesis), by a three-lane machine-checked route: a graph-to-profile bridge bijection (Finset.card_bij), a transfer-matrix packaging (T = A.B on five even-column profiles, with joint induction giving z(2k+1) = sum(T^k 1) and z(2k+2) = sum(T^k vec0)), and an algebraic reduction via the certificate polynomial p(x) = x^3 - 12x^2 + 15x - 2 with the two decide-closed certificates p(T)1 = 0 and p(T)vec0 = 0 (the only boundary case, n = 6, is a decide-closed integer identity). The proof compiles with no sorry; #print axioms for c_z_rec is [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] (exactly the whitelist). Novelty adjudication, copied from the pipeline's proposition-level C9 exclusivity review included here in full with every zero-hit query (32 networked query strings over OEIS/arXiv/Crossref/MSE with positive controls, plus 6 local GitHub and 4 mathlib sweeps; independent re-verification confirmed): no occupying record for the sequence z(n), its odd-indexed subsequence, or the defective-strip object; the even-indexed subsequence coincides term-by-term with the registered A122011 (a 3x3 matrix-power example with no graph-theoretic content), and the recurrence signature (12,-15,2) is already indexed in the OEIS linear-recurrence index - so the claim is strictly new sequence (lower tier), never new mathematics and never a new recurrence. The literature-layer zero-hit verdict is limited to arXiv + Crossref + MSE. Claim note under CC-BY-4.0, code under MIT. Produced by the AI4Math pipeline (LLM generation + Lean kernel adjudication; task budgets copied verbatim from the task ledger: 8 of 16 permitted agent-run samples, 0 of 8 llm-calls, 10 of 36 strict kernel compiles plus separately-ledgered compile-debug probes; this note consumed 0 pipeline LLM calls against a cap of 4). The human author reviewed all evidence and is responsible for the content; the AI system is not an author. The narrative paper of this result is prepared separately under the pipeline's paper lane and will reference this DOI.
